title: Distance from Goslar, Germany to Hildesheim, Germany - Travelmath
content: The total straight line flight distance from Goslar, Germany to Hildesheim, Germany is 26 miles. This is equivalent to 42 kilometers or 23 nautical miles.

title: How far is it? - Straight Line Distance Calculator - GPS Coordinates
content: # How far is it? This tool enables you to calculate the straight line **distance between** two locations or two cities, "as the crow flies". As you can share your location, it will let you know easily how far you are in a straight line from any point of interest. Here are the steps to use it:. 1. Enter the address or the city of the first location. 2. Enter the address or the city of the second location. 3. Click on the "Calculate the distance" button. **How far is it?** The result of the geodesic distance calculation is immediately displayed, along with a map showing the two points linked by a straight line. Our formula integrates the curve of the earth to calculate as best as possible the distance as the crow flies. It is extremely accurate, especially for shorter distances. Click on the button to use your geolocation instead of manually entering an address. LoaderAllow or deny location access to proceed.

title: Calculate distance and bearing between two Latitude/Longitude ...
content: This uses the ‘**haversine**’ formula to calculate the great-circle distance between two points – that is, the shortest distance over the earth’s surface – giving an ‘as-the-crow-flies’ distance between the points (ignoring any hills they fly over, of course!). | Haversine formula: | a = sin²(Δφ/2) + cos φ1 ⋅ cos φ2 ⋅ sin²(Δλ/2) |. | JavaScript: | ``` const R = 6371e3; // metres const φ1 = lat1 * Math.PI/180; // φ, λ in radians const φ2 = lat2 * Math.PI/180; const Δφ = (lat2-lat1) * Math.PI/180; const Δλ = (lon2-lon1) * Math.PI/180; const a = Math.sin(Δφ/2) * Math.sin(Δφ/2) + Math.cos(φ1) * Math.cos(φ2) * Math.sin(Δλ/2) * Math.sin(Δλ/2); const c = 2 * Math.atan2(Math.sqrt(a), Math.sqrt(1-a)); const d = R * c; // in metres ``` |. | Law of cosines: | d = acos( sin φ1 ⋅ sin φ2 + cos φ1 ⋅ cos φ2 ⋅ cos Δλ ) ⋅ R |.
